The installation failed because **your disk is completely full** (`No space left on device` / `os error 28`). 

Checking disk usage reveals only **~133 MB** of available storage left on the APFS container shared by your volumes:

```text

/dev/disk3s5    460Gi  393Gi  133Mi     100%  /System/Volumes/Data
/dev/disk3s8    460Gi   11Gi  133Mi      99%  /Users/chrisdoc/fun
```

When `pnpm` attempted to download and extract large packages (such as `@effect/tsgo-darwin-arm64` ~94MB and `@cloudflare/workerd-darwin-arm64` ~38MB), it hit the disk limit.

---

### Why the pnpm store warning happened

`/Users/chrisdoc/fun` is mounted on its own APFS volume (`/dev/disk3s8`), separate from the main data volume (`/dev/disk3s5`). 

Because hardlinks cannot cross filesystem/volume boundaries, `pnpm` cannot link packages from `~/Library/pnpm/store/v11` into projects inside `~/fun`. As a result, `pnpm` created a second store at `~/fun/.pnpm-store/v11`. Both stores are currently taking up **~6.9 GB each** from the same shared APFS disk container.

---

### Quick ways to reclaim space

Here are safe caches and locations you can clean right away to free up **~15–20 GB**:

#### 1. Empty Trash (~2.7 GB)
```sh
rm -rf ~/.Trash/*
```
*(or right-click Trash in the Dock and select "Empty Trash")*

#### 2. Clean Homebrew and mise caches (~8.9 GB)
```sh
brew cleanup --prune=all
mise cache clear
```

#### 3. Prune pnpm stores
Prune unreferenced packages in the current project's store:
```sh
pnpm store prune
```

#### 4. (Optional) Avoid duplicate pnpm stores
If most of your development repositories live under `~/fun`, you can tell `pnpm` to always use `~/fun/.pnpm-store`:
```sh
pnpm config set store-dir /Users/chrisdoc/fun/.pnpm-store/v11
rm -rf ~/Library/pnpm/store
```
*(This alone frees **~6.9 GB** by removing the duplicate store on the other volume).*

---

Once you have freed up disk space, run:
```sh
pnpm i
```
